extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, litigants, and parties considering or involved in Covered Business Method (CBM) proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the Transitional Program for Covered Business Method Patents (TPCBM): what patents are covered, who may file a petition, which procedures and standards apply, key dates, and where to find the governing rules and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — applies only to covered business method patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure for conducting TPCBM review took effect on September 16, 2012, but only applies to covered business method patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is limited to patents that meet the statutory/ regulatory definition of a 'covered business method' (see 'Covered Business Method and Technological Invention Definitions Final Rules' referenced on the page). Parties should confirm a patent qualifies as a CBM before pursuing a TPCBM petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to file — must have been sued or charged with infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may not file a petition for a TPCBM proceeding unless the person or the person's real party in interest or privy has been sued for infringement of the patent or charged with infringement under the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standing for filing is limited to accused infringers (or their real parties in interest/privies). Mere interest in the patent, or desire to challenge it outside the context of litigation, does not confer filing eligibility. Petitioners should document the relevant litigation or charge when filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural framework — uses post grant review standards and procedures with exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: TPCBM proceedings employ the standards and procedures of a post grant review, with certain exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat TPCBM largely like a Post-Grant Review (PGR) in terms of timing, motions, discovery, and PTAB procedures, but identify and account for the enumerated exceptions (see page and referenced rules). Counsel should consult the PGR rules and the specific CBM exceptions when preparing petitions and responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art availability exception for first-to-invent patents
rubrics_metrics.description: For example, for first to invent patents only a subset of prior art is available to support the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike typical PGR where broad categories of prior art may be asserted, first-to-invent (pre-AIA) patents face a narrower universe of prior art that can be relied upon in a TPCBM. Petitioners must verify which prior-art classes are permitted and tailor grounds accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure for conducting TPCBM review took effect on September 16, 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the date when the TPCBM regime and its governing rules became effective. Challenges to patents based on events or filings tied to dates before/after this effective date may implicate transitional rules; practitioners should be aware of temporal applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program sunset for new petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The program will sunset for new TPCBM petitions on September 16, 2020.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new TPCBM petitions could be filed after the sunset date. Parties evaluating remedies or strategies must account for the unavailability of new CBM petitions after that date (though existing proceedings or other review mechanisms may remain relevant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative governing rules and guidance (Federal Register and Trial Practice Guide)
rubrics_metrics.description: General Administrative Trial Final Rules (77 Fed. Reg. 48612, August 14, 2012); Trial Practice Guide (77 Fed. Reg. 48756, August 14, 2012); Inter Partes, Post Grant, and Covered Business Method Review Final Rules (77 Fed. Reg. 48680, August 14, 2012); Covered Business Method and Technological Invention Definitions Final Rules (77 Fed. Reg. 48734, August 14, 2012); Proposed Rule of Practice for Trials before the PTAB (77 Fed. Reg. 6879, Feb. 9, 2012); Proposed Trial Practice Guide (77 Fed. Reg. 6868, Feb. 9, 2012); Proposed Rules for the Transitional Program for Covered Business Methods (77 Fed. Reg. 7080, February 10, 2012); Proposed Rule for the Technological Invention Definition (77 Fed. Reg. 7095, February 10, 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Federal Register notices and the Trial Practice Guide collectively set out the detailed procedures, definitions, and practice expectations for TPCBM proceedings. Practitioners should consult the cited final rules and practice guide for text of requirements, filing deadlines, claim construction principles, motion practice, and other procedural details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources — FAQs, implementation timeline, and P-TACTS for case search
rubrics_metrics.description: 12 Month Implementation Timeline; Transitional Program for Covered Business Method Patents FAQs; To search for an CBM, click on the system link for P-TACTS. Additional information is located on the P-TACTS information page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO provides FAQs and an implementation timeline to clarify common questions and transitional issues. Use P-TACTS to locate existing CBM/TPCBM dockets and precedential decisions to guide strategy and understand how the Board has applied rules in practice.
